questions.q: Name two E. coli strains commonly used for routine cloning and state one key genotype feature each that makes them suitable.
questions.a: DH5α (genotype: recA1, endA1, hsdR17, lacZΔM15) — recA1 prevents plasmid rearrangement; HB101 (recA13, hsdR20, lacY1) — hsdR20 disables restriction for better transformation. A wrong answer (e.g., naming BL21 for routine cloning) reveals the student confuses expression strains (DE3 lysogen) with cloning strains, or cannot link genotype markers to their phenotypic benefits.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the hsdR mutation is critical when transforming E. coli with plasmid DNA isolated from a different bacterial species.
questions.a: hsdR encodes the restriction subunit of the type I restriction-modification system; an hsdR mutation (e.g., hsdR17) makes the strain restriction-deficient (r⁻) but modification-proficient (m⁺), so incoming unmethylated foreign plasmid DNA is not recognized as "non-self" and degraded. A wrong answer (e.g., "hsdR increases transformation efficiency by making cells competent") shows the student conflates restriction deficiency with chemical competence, missing the molecular mechanism of host restriction.

questions.q: You have a high-copy plasmid (pUC19 derivative) that gives poor yield in HB101 but excellent yield in DH5α. Both strains are recA⁻ and hsdR⁻. Propose the most likely genotypic difference responsible and justify.
questions.a: DH5α carries endA1 (endonuclease I deficiency) while HB101 is endA⁺. Endonuclease I degrades plasmid DNA during alkaline lysis prep, reducing yield. The student must identify endA as the differentiating marker and explain its role in plasmid purification. A wrong answer (e.g., blaming lacZ or recA) indicates failure to connect endA to plasmid quality during miniprep.

questions.q: Compare DH5α and BL21(DE3) for two distinct cloning scenarios: (a) propagating a recombinant plasmid for sequencing, (b) expressing a toxic protein under T7 promoter. Which strain for which scenario, and why?
questions.a: (a) DH5α — recA1 ensures plasmid stability, endA1 gives clean DNA, lacZΔM15 allows blue-white screening. (b) BL21(DE3) — carries λ DE3 lysogen (T7 RNA polymerase under lacUV5), lacks lon and ompT proteases for protein stability, but is recA⁺ and endA⁺ so plasmid may rearrange/degrade. A wrong assignment (e.g., using BL21 for plasmid prep) shows inability to distinguish cloning vs. expression strain design.

questions.q: A student argues: "Since JM109 and DH5α both have recA1 and lacZΔM15, they are interchangeable for all cloning purposes." Evaluate this claim with two specific counterexamples.
questions.a: Claim is false. (1) JM109 is endA⁺ (has endonuclease I) while DH5α is endA1 — plasmid preps from JM109 may be sheared. (2) JM109 is hsdR⁺ (restriction-proficient) while DH5α is hsdR17 — transformation of unmethylated DNA (e.g., from PCR or eukaryotic source) will be inefficient in JM109. A weak evaluation that only mentions "they are similar" misses these critical functional differences.

questions.q: Design a genotype for a custom E. coli strain optimized for cloning AT-rich, unstable inserts from a eukaryotic genome. List five mutations you would include and the specific problem each solves.
questions.a: Example answer: recA1 (prevents recombination of repetitive AT-rich sequences), endA1 (clean plasmid yield), hsdR17 (accepts unmethylated eukaryotic DNA), gyrA96 (nalidixic acid resistance for counter-selection), and lacZΔM15 (blue-white screening). Additional valid mutations: mcrA/mcrBC/mrr (for methylated DNA), tonA (phage T1 resistance). A poor answer lists random markers without linking each to AT-rich/eukaryotic DNA challenges.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: E. coli is the most widely used prokaryotic host for gene cloning due to its well-characterized genetics, rapid growth (doubling time ~20 min), high ______ efficiency, and ability to maintain plasmid vectors; specific laboratory strains (e.g., DH5α, HB101, JM109) carry mutations such as recA1 (reduces recombination), endA1 (lacks endonuclease I for better plasmid yield), and hsdR17 (defective restriction-modification system) that enhance cloning stability and plasmid quality.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you have just cut your gene of interest and a plasmid vector with EcoRI, ligated them, and now you need to transform bacteria to amplify the ______ plasmid.
What is E. coli? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: E. coli is the most widely used prokaryotic host for gene cloning due to its well-characterized genetics, rapid growth (doubling time ~20 min), high transformation efficiency, and ability to maintain plasmid vectors; specific laboratory strains (e.g., DH5α, HB101, JM109) carry mutations such as recA1 (reduces recombination), endA1 (lacks.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about E. coli?
questions.a: Students often think "any E. coli strain works for cloning" and pick BL21(DE3) for routine plasmid propagation because it's "common in the lab." They miss that BL21 is an expression strain: it is recA⁺ (so plasmids rearrange), endA⁺ (poor miniprep quality), and hsdR⁺ (restricts foreign DNA).

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can list at least three common E. coli cloning strains, write their key genotype markers (recA, endA, hsdR, lacZΔM15, etc.), and explain how each mutation improves plasmid propagation or cloning efficiency.
